name: TrackKaro Pakistan – Courier Tracking & COD
author: DANGO Solutions

sections.description:
TrackKaro is a serviceware plugin. It connects your WooCommerce store to the TrackKaro platform (https://trackkaro.pk), an external paid SaaS service operated by DANGO Solutions. All courier API connections, status polling, and tracking data processing happen on the TrackKaro servers — not locally on your WordPress installation. A TrackKaro account is required; new accounts include a free trial.

Pakistani e-commerce stores lose hours every week manually checking courier websites and copy-pasting tracking numbers into order notes. TrackKaro fixes that.

Connect your WooCommerce store once, and TrackKaro automatically polls your courier APIs in the background, updates every order’s status, notifies your customers, and marks orders complete the moment a delivery is confirmed — all without you lifting a finger.

Supported Couriers:

  • ✅ PostEx
  • ✅ TCS
  • ✅ Leopards Courier
  • ✅ CallCourier
  • ✅ Sonic / Trax
  • ✅ DEX (Daraz Express) — tracking only
  • ✅ Daewoo FastEx
  • ✅ M&P Courier

A free TrackKaro account is required. Sign up at trackkaro.pk to start your free trial.

Why TrackKaro?

Pakistan’s courier APIs are fragmented, inconsistent, and go down without warning. TrackKaro’s server layer normalises statuses across all couriers into one clean format, handles retries, and keeps your store’s data accurate even when a courier API is having a bad day. You get dedicated tracking infrastructure without building or maintaining any of it yourself.

Key Features:

Automatic Status Sync

TrackKaro polls your couriers in the background via WP-Cron. Statuses update from “In Transit” to “Out for Delivery” to “Delivered” automatically — no manual refreshes.

Branded Customer Tracking Page

Every order gets a tracking page on your own domain. Customers click the link in their order email and see the full delivery timeline — your store name, your colours, your brand.

Real-Time Leopards Push Updates

Leopards Courier can push status updates to TrackKaro the moment they happen (no polling lag). Your orders update within seconds of a courier scan.

Courier Order Creation

Create shipment bookings with PostEx and Leopards directly from the WooCommerce order screen — COD, prepaid, and zero-value orders all supported. No need to log into courier portals.

Bulk Tracking Import

Got a spreadsheet of tracking numbers? Import them all at once via CSV. TrackKaro creates jobs for each one and starts syncing immediately.

Auto-Complete Orders on Delivery

When a parcel is delivered, TrackKaro can automatically mark the WooCommerce order as Completed.

Order List Tracking Column

See every order’s live courier status right in the WooCommerce Orders list.

Dashboard Widget

A quick-glance widget on your WordPress dashboard shows active shipments, deliveries this month, and your delivery rate.

Customer Status Email Notifications

Optionally send automated email updates to customers when their parcel moves to key milestones (dispatched, out for delivery, delivered). Works via TrackKaro’s mail server or your own SMTP.

HPOS Compatible

Fully compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (custom order tables). Tested with WooCommerce 5.0 through 9.x.

How It Works:

  1. Install the plugin and activate it on your WooCommerce store.
  2. Sign up for a free TrackKaro account at trackkaro.pk (takes 2 minutes).
  3. Copy your API token from the TrackKaro dashboard and paste it into WooCommerce → TrackKaro Settings.
  4. Done. Add a tracking number to any order and TrackKaro takes it from there.

Your free trial includes a set number of tracking jobs so you can test with real orders before subscribing.

Pricing:

TrackKaro uses a prepaid credit model billed in PKR. Buy a plan that fits your monthly order volume. No hidden fees. No long-term contracts. See current plans at trackkaro.pk.

External Services

This plugin is SERVICEWARE. It has no standalone tracking functionality — it is a connector to the TrackKaro external platform. All courier tracking, status polling, API calls to courier companies, and shipment management are processed exclusively on TrackKaro’s servers. None of this processing can be replicated locally by the plugin code itself.

A paid account with TrackKaro is required. New accounts receive a free trial, but continued use requires a prepaid PKR credit plan purchased at https://trackkaro.pk. The API key that connects this plugin to the service is obtained only after signing up.

This plugin connects to the TrackKaro platform (operated by DANGO Solutions, https://solutions.dango.pk) to provide all courier tracking and order management functionality. This connection is mandatory — the plugin cannot function without it, as all courier API communication and data processing occurs on the TrackKaro servers, not locally on your WordPress site.

Service details:

  • Service name: TrackKaro
  • Service URL: https://trackkaro.pk
  • API endpoint: https://trackkaro.pk/api/v1/
  • Operated by: DANGO Solutions (https://solutions.dango.pk)
  • Privacy Policy: https://trackkaro.pk/page/privacy-policy
  • Terms of Service: https://trackkaro.pk/page/terms-of-service

What data is sent and when:

  1. On every tracking sync (every ~5 minutes for active orders): The plugin sends your WooCommerce order’s tracking number, courier name, and an internal order reference to the TrackKaro server. The server queries the courier’s API and returns the current status, location, and event history.

  2. On plugin activation and settings save: Your store’s domain and the API token you entered are sent to TrackKaro to verify the connection. No customer data is included.

  3. On courier order creation (PostEx / Leopards): When you create a shipment booking from the WooCommerce order screen, the customer’s name, phone number, delivery address, order amount, and parcel details are sent to TrackKaro, which forwards them to the courier’s booking API to create the shipment. This transmission only occurs when you explicitly click the “Generate Courier Order” button.

  4. On customer email notifications (if enabled): The customer’s email address (stored on the order) may be sent to TrackKaro’s mail server to deliver tracking update emails. This feature is off by default and must be explicitly enabled by the shop owner.

What is NOT sent: Payment details, billing addresses, card numbers, or any information beyond what is listed above. TrackKaro acts solely as a tracking and logistics coordination service.

No tracking functionality can be performed locally — this plugin is specifically designed to work with the TrackKaro external service. If you do not agree to the TrackKaro Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, this plugin is not suitable for your store.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress dashboard go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload the trackkar-woo.zip file and click Install Now.
  3. Activate the plugin.
  4. Go to WooCommerce → TrackKaro Settings.
  5. Paste your API token from your TrackKaro dashboard.
  6. Click Save Settings. The plugin will verify your token and confirm the connection.
  7. Open any WooCommerce order and add a tracking number — TrackKaro will start syncing within the next cron cycle (typically within 5 minutes).

First time? Create your free account at trackkaro.pk before step 4.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin work without a TrackKaro account?

No. TrackKaro is a SaaS platform — the plugin is the bridge between your WooCommerce store and the TrackKaro server, which handles all courier API connections, status normalisation, and background polling. You need a TrackKaro account to use it. New accounts include a free trial so you can evaluate the platform with real shipments before paying anything.

Is a subscription required?

You start with a free trial. Once your trial quota is used, you purchase a prepaid PKR plan. Plans are available at trackkaro.pk. There is no monthly subscription lock-in — you buy credit when you need it.

Which couriers are supported?

PostEx, TCS, Leopards Courier, CallCourier, Sonic/Trax, DEX (Daraz Express, tracking only), and Daewoo FastEx. More couriers are added based on demand — contact support if yours is missing.

Do I need to add my own courier API credentials?

Not necessarily. TrackKaro maintains central API credentials for most couriers, which your store can use out of the box. If you have your own API keys (e.g. a dedicated PostEx or Leopards account), you can add them in your TrackKaro dashboard for direct access.

Will this slow down my store?

No. The plugin loads only on admin pages and offloads all tracking work to WP-Cron background jobs. There is zero impact on your storefront or checkout speed.

What is the branded tracking page?

When a customer clicks the tracking link in their order email, they land on a page on your own domain (e.g. yourstore.com/track-your-order/) that shows the full delivery timeline in your store’s branding. TrackKaro automatically creates this page on plugin activation.

Can I create courier bookings through the plugin?

Yes — for PostEx and Leopards Courier. Open the WooCommerce order, fill in the parcel details, and submit the booking directly from the order screen. The booking reference is saved to the order automatically.

Is it compatible with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)?

Yes. TrackKaro is fully compatible with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage (custom order tables) and has been tested with WooCommerce 5.0 through 9.x.

My tracking status isn’t updating — what do I check?

  1. Confirm WP-Cron is running (check Tools → Scheduled Actions or use a cron monitoring plugin).
  2. Check your quota in WooCommerce → TrackKaro Settings — if you’ve used your plan’s allowance, new syncs are paused.
  3. Visit your TrackKaro dashboard for detailed tracking logs and diagnostic tools.

Where can I get support?

Open a ticket at trackkaro.pk/panel/tickets or email support@dango.pk .
sections.changelog:
1.0.97

  • Fixed: M&P parcels were booked at a heavier weight than you entered — 0.5 kg was sent as 1 kg, moving every small parcel into the next charging band. M&P accepts decimal weights; TrackKaro now sends exactly what you type.
  • Added: The weight box on Bulk Create follows each courier’s own unit, so you never confirm a weight the courier will change behind you.
  • Fixed: M&P airway bills print three labels to a sheet instead of one, and no longer print three copies of the same parcel by default.

1.0.96

  • Changed: Amounts to collect are whole rupees now — no more “.00” on every row.
  • Fixed: After booking a batch with a courier that issues no load sheet or airway bill (M&P, TCS, InstaWorld), the window said “generate the paperwork below” above an empty space. It now says what actually happened.
  • Changed: The batch table fits without scrolling sideways on a normal screen, and the Result column no longer gets squeezed off the edge.
  • Fixed: M&P pickup locations were always an empty dropdown, on both the order screen and Bulk Create. The cause was on the TrackKaro side and is fixed there — no settings change needed; your locations now appear, and the one you used last is pre-selected.
  • Changed: If your TrackKaro plan runs out mid-batch, Bulk Create now stops and says so once, leaving the remaining orders untouched, instead of failing every row with the same message.
  • Fixed: Downloading Airway Bills for a bulk batch stopped at 10 orders and refused the rest. There is no 10-order limit any more — ask for the whole batch and you get every label (as one PDF, or a zip when the courier cannot fit them all on one document).
  • Added: Bulk Create can now pass the customer’s own checkout note (“call before delivery”) to the courier as Special Instructions, per order. Off by default, remembered once you set it, and it tells you how many orders in the batch actually have a note.

1.0.95

  • Fixed: An order you typed in yourself from WooCommerce → Orders has no payment method, so Bulk Create read it as already paid and booked it with nothing to collect — you delivered the goods and the rider brought back no money. Bulk Create now asks whether the order has actually been paid, not which gateway it used.
  • Added: Every row in Bulk Create now shows the order total (paid orders included) and the amount to collect at the door in a field you can edit before booking. Change it for a partial advance, a discount agreed on the phone, or anything the order total does not reflect; the change is written to the order notes.
  • Added: A row set to collect nothing while money is still owed is highlighted in amber, so it can never happen by accident.
  • Changed: The Bulk Create window is wider with a header that stays put while you scroll, so the city and the amount are readable at the same time.
  • Added: Bulk Create Courier Orders now offers the Load Sheet (and Airway Bills, up to the courier limit of 10 parcels) right in the window as soon as the batch is booked — no need to close it and find the orders again.
  • Changed: Closing the bulk window no longer re-ticks the orders you just booked. It could only do that reliably on the full orders list, so anyone working inside a saved filter got a partial selection back.

1.0.94

  • Added: TCS is now available for booking courier orders — on the order screen and in Bulk Create — not just for tracking. Pick your TCS pickup location once at the top of the bulk window and it is remembered for next time.

1.0.93

  • Fixed: Twelve labels on the Bulk Create screen — including the “Weight (kg)” column heading and the shipping-details panel — could not be translated, because they were never registered for translation. They always showed in English regardless of site language.

1.0.92

  • Added: Bulk Create Courier Orders now fills in the courier city for you wherever it can match it — including common misspellings (“Faislabad”), abbreviations (“LHR”, “Khi”), and cities spelled correctly further along the delivery address. A line at the top tells you how many were filled in.
  • Added: Any city we filled in from anything less than an exact name match is highlighted in amber with the reason underneath, so you only check the rows that need you. The highlight clears as soon as you pick a city yourself.
  • Fixed: The Payment column showed “₨5,202” instead of “₨5,202” — the currency symbol was being printed as raw HTML code.
  • Fixed: The Payment column split the amount across three stacked lines. The amount and what happens to it now read as one line, and paid orders show which payment method was used.

1.0.91

  • Fixed: Test Connection reported an invalid API key after you saved your settings, even though the key was correct and everything else kept working. The API Token box was a password field, so browsers autofilled it with your saved WordPress login password on every page reload — Test Connection then tested that instead of your token. The box is now a normal text field and refuses autofill.
  • Fixed: Test Connection now checks the token looks like a TrackKaro token before contacting the server, and tells you if it does not, instead of returning a bare “invalid key”.
  • Fixed: Clicking Test Connection with an empty API Token box no longer ignores the token already saved in your settings.

1.0.90

  • Added: Bulk Create Courier Orders now asks for your shipping details once, at the top of the window — pickup address, origin city and so on for the courier you picked. It remembers them for next time and collapses to a single line, so the orders list keeps the space. Previously bulk could only reuse whatever a single order screen had saved, so a courier you had never booked from an order screen failed on every row with no way to fix it from there.
  • Added: Weight is now editable per order in the bulk window, starting from the product weights on the order. Bulk used to send a fixed weight for every parcel regardless of what was in the box.
  • Added: “Close & Reload” after a bulk booking closes the window, refreshes the orders list, and keeps the orders you just booked ticked — so you can go straight to Load Sheet or Airway Bill without finding and re-selecting them all.
  • Fixed: Bulk booking with Trax (Sonic) or Leopards failed with “City is required” even though the city was clearly selected in the row.
  • Fixed: Couriers you have not added API keys for are now shown greyed out with the reason, instead of silently disappearing from the bulk window or being fully selectable on the order screen. You could previously fill in an entire order for a courier you had no key for and only be told at the end.
  • Removed: The “Special Instructions” box in the bulk window. One line applied to every order in a batch is not per-order information, and Leopards orders get a sensible default automatically.
  • Removed: The “Default Courier for Bulk Orders” setting. The bulk window already remembers the courier you used last time, so there was nothing to configure.
  • Removed: The “Leopards Courier — Default Shipper Details” settings section. The order screen already remembers your origin city, shipper and details from the last order you booked, and your shipper address comes from your WooCommerce store address. Nothing to fill in twice.
  • Changed: The bulk window is wider and the orders table scrolls on its own, so the buttons never get pushed off screen.

1.0.89

  • Changed: the first-run “show trust badge” prompt no longer relies on WordPress’s bundled jQuery UI. It is now a small self-contained box, so a future WordPress release cannot break it.
  • Added: your store now tells TrackKaro which platform it is, so shipments from WooCommerce, OpenCart and other stores are told apart in your TrackKaro reports.

1.0.88

  • Added: Bulk Create Courier Orders now shows each order’s payment type, amount, phone number and status, and lets you untick individual orders before booking. One click deselects every already-paid order.
  • Fixed: an order that was already paid online was being booked with its full amount as cash-on-delivery, so the courier would have collected the money a second time. Paid orders now book with nothing to collect, on both the bulk screen and the single-order box (still editable there).
  • Removed: CallCourier. The company has closed, so it no longer appears anywhere in the plugin.
  • Added: Nexus Global Logistics is now a supported courier. Pick it on an order, or let TrackKaro track it automatically — tracking needs no API key, because Nexus does not issue any. Their tracking link works as a one-click link for your customers.
  • Fixed: courier bookings from stores whose shipping address is set to “Default to customer billing address” (or that force billing, or sell virtual goods) were sent with a blank delivery address. Address, city, phone and name are now taken from whichever of the shipping or billing details is actually filled in, field by field, and a booking with no address at all is refused instead of shipped nowhere.
  • Fixed: in Bulk Create Courier Orders, the Create button stayed disabled after a run, so rows that failed could not be retried without reloading and re-selecting every order. It now comes back as “Retry remaining rows” and skips the orders that already booked.
  • Fixed: a row whose city could not be matched to the courier’s own city list reported “City is required” while the dropdown plainly showed a city. Rows missing a city are now flagged before anything is sent, and a city that cannot be matched is named in the error.
  • Fixed: saving settings only cleared PostEx’s cached city list. All couriers’ city lists are now refreshed, so a bad or outdated list no longer survives for up to 30 days.

1.0.87

  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1.

1.0.86

  • Added: if you switch on “Auto Shipping Charges at Checkout” here but haven’t finished setting it up on TrackKaro, the plugin now tells you so on your settings and WooCommerce screens, with a direct link to the right page. Previously the feature simply stayed silent and checkout kept showing your flat rate with no explanation.

1.0.85

  • Added: InstaWorld support. You can now book InstaWorld shipments from an order screen or in bulk, cancel a booking before it is collected, and follow every scan on your tracking page. Pick the destination city from InstaWorld’s own list; there is no pickup address to choose, because InstaWorld collects from the address registered on your InstaWorld account.

1.0.84

  • Fixed: automatic status syncing could silently stop on some stores, with “Cron reschedule event error … Event schedule does not exist” appearing in the server error log. The plugin’s custom sync intervals are now registered on every request, and any store whose sync had already been unscheduled by this bug repairs itself on the next page load.
  • Changed: when the delivery-charge estimate is switched off for your account, the plugin now remembers that for 6 hours instead of 15 minutes. It still refreshes immediately when you save settings or turn the estimate on, and this removes a steady stream of needless requests to the TrackKaro server.

1.0.83

  • Added: a clear notice on the WooCommerce and TrackKaro screens when automatic tracking has been paused for a courier because your TrackKaro account has no API credentials for it. It names the courier, tells you how many orders are affected, confirms nothing is lost, and links straight to the page where you add your keys. Previously those orders just stopped updating with no explanation.

1.0.82

  • Fixed: pressing “Save Settings” now always refreshes courier, quota and checkout data from the TrackKaro server. Previously nothing was refreshed unless you actually changed a value, so a courier you had just enabled in your TrackKaro panel could take up to 24 hours to appear in the booking screens.

1.0.81

  • Added: a single “Mark as Dispatched” tick in the Bulk Create Courier Orders popup that applies to the whole batch, matching the checkbox on the single-order booking form. Your choice is remembered and shared between both screens.
  • Fixed: the “Default Courier for Bulk Orders” option the popup points you to was missing from the settings screen — it is now shown under Features.
  • Fixed: bulk “Download Airway Bills” / “Download Load Sheet” tried to open a new tab, which most browsers block. The document now downloads as a file straight to your computer without leaving the Orders list.

1.0.80

  • Improved: the Bulk Create Courier Orders popup now shows each customer’s delivery address exactly as they entered it, including their city, so you can spot and correct a wrong city before booking.

1.0.79

  • Improved: courier names and courier tracking links now come from your TrackKaro account instead of being fixed in the plugin, so new couriers and corrected tracking links appear automatically without waiting for a plugin update.
  • Fixed: DEX and Trax orders could show no “Track on courier site” link in some places.

1.0.78

  • Added: M&P (Muller & Phipps) courier support — track M&P shipments, book M&P orders from the order screen (destination city, pickup location, Overnight/Second Day service, insurance and fragile options), and include M&P in Bulk Create Courier Orders.

1.0.77

  • Fixed: The bulk “Download Airway Bills” / “Download Load Sheet” actions now open the document in a new tab instead of navigating your orders list away from WooCommerce. If your browser blocks the popup, a link is shown so you can open it yourself.
  • Changed: “Apply Shipping Charges To” now covers all of your enabled payment methods when you haven’t picked any, so a new install works with just the checkout estimate toggle turned on, and payment methods you add later are included automatically.
  • Changed: Clarified that automatic shipping charges at checkout work with Leopards and Trax (Sonic), not Leopards alone.

1.0.76

  • Added: Bulk Create Courier Orders now supports Trax (Sonic) alongside PostEx and Leopards, reusing your account’s last-used Sonic pickup address the same way PostEx/Leopards defaults already work.
  • Added: “Courier City” (Checkout City Selector) and the shipping-charge estimate now also work on WooCommerce Blocks checkout, not just the classic checkout form.

1.0.75

  • Added: New order-list bulk action “TrackKaro: Bulk Create Courier Orders” — select multiple orders that don’t have a tracking number yet, pick a courier (PostEx or Leopards), review/edit the delivery city per order in a popup, and book them all at once. Uses your account’s saved pickup address / shipper defaults, so nothing extra to set up first.

1.0.74

  • Added: New order-list bulk actions “TrackKaro: Download Airway Bills” and “TrackKaro: Download Load Sheet” — select multiple orders booked with the same courier and download one combined PDF. Selecting orders from more than one courier is rejected with a clear message instead of guessing.

1.0.73

  • Added: New “Checkout City Selector” option — adds an optional “Courier City” dropdown at checkout so customers pick their city from the courier’s own list, giving you clean, courier-recognised cities on every order. Enable it in Settings and per-courier in your TrackKaro panel under “City Selector”. Off by default.
  • Fixed: “Email the store owner once when an order first fails delivery” now defaults to on for new installs, matching the plugin’s other delivery-status notification defaults.

1.0.72

  • Improved: The pickup address is now remembered between orders, the same way the pickup city already was. If you change the pickup city it clears itself, so an address from the wrong city can never be used by mistake.

1.0.71

  • Added: DEX (Daraz Express) now appears in the courier list on the order screen, so you can add a DEX tracking number and have it tracked automatically. (Tracking only – DEX orders cannot be booked from WooCommerce yet.)

1.0.70

  • Added: DEX (Daraz Express) tracking numbers now link to the DEX tracking page from the order screen and customer emails.

1.0.69

  • Improved: The address check is no longer a second button competing with “Generate Courier Order” — the check still runs automatically when you generate the order, and a small “Check this address first” link is there for when you want the courier’s verdict without booking.

1.0.68

  • Added: Address check before booking — for couriers that support it (currently Trax/Sonic), the courier is asked about the delivery address first. If it has anything to flag (out of service area, a poor delivery history for that customer, and so on) you see a plain-English note and decide whether to book anyway.
  • Added: Courier notes stay visible against the order — even if you check the address and choose not to book, the courier’s note is kept on the order so you and your team can see it later.
  • Added: Any note the courier returns while booking is shown right after the order is created.

1.0.67

  • Fixed: “Download Airway Bill” and “Download Load Sheet” no longer get blocked by the browser’s popup blocker — the document now opens reliably in a new tab (previously affected Trax/Sonic in particular). If a browser still blocks it, a clickable link is shown so you can open it manually.
  • Improved: If a courier cannot provide a load sheet or airway bill yet (for example, before the shipment is picked up), you now see a clear, readable reason instead of a raw error.

1.0.66

  • Added: The “COD Order Created” box now shows the courier name alongside the tracking number.
  • Fixed: Trax (Sonic) orders now show the “Download Airway Bill” and “Download Load Sheet” buttons, same as PostEx and Leopards.
  • Fixed: Billing & Account panel now labels a free trial and a free plan correctly, shows the real number of shipments tracked, and shows the trial’s remaining credits and days left instead of “unlimited”.
  • Changed: “Trax (Sonic)” is now labelled consistently everywhere (was “Sonic/Trax”).
  • Changed: “Alert on First Failed Delivery” is now enabled by default for new installs so you never miss a failed delivery.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.0.2.

1.0.65

  • Added: When a shipment is cancelled with the courier before it is dispatched, the tracking number is now removed from the WooCommerce order automatically, so cancelled orders no longer show a dead tracking number in your orders list.
  • Changed: If the parcel is already in transit, the courier turns the request into a return — tracking is kept active so you can follow the return leg. The order note now says which of the two happened.

1.0.64

  • Fixed: PostEx “Order Type” now sends the value “Reverse” (per the official PostEx API specification) instead of “Reversed”. Normal and Replacement orders are unaffected.

1.0.63

  • Changed: Leopards booking form now has a Shipper dropdown that defaults to “Self” — your main Leopards merchant account — exactly like the Leopards portal’s own Book Packet form. Previously a saved Shipper Sys ID could silently book every order under a sub-shipper profile instead of your main account.
  • Added: Registered sub-shippers from your Leopards account now load automatically into the Shipper dropdown, so you can still pick one per order when needed.
  • Fixed: Orders can no longer be booked under an unintended ad-hoc shipper name — manual shipper details are only sent when you explicitly choose “Custom” in the Shipper dropdown.

1.0.62

  • Fixed: The automatic courier shipping charge no longer replaces the store’s shipping method with a custom one — it now adjusts the existing shipping rate’s cost and label in place. This fixes Cash on Delivery disappearing from the payment options (and orders being saved with the flat rate) on stores where COD is restricted to specific shipping methods, and fixes the checkout appearing stuck when changing the destination city.

1.0.61

  • Internal: Removed the plugin’s hardcoded courier reference for the checkout shipping-charge estimate — the TrackKaro server already resolves which courier’s estimate to use per store, so the plugin no longer needs to know or send it. No visible change in behavior.

1.0.60

  • Changed: The checkout shipping line for the automatic courier charge is now labeled “Shipping Charges” (previously “Estimated Courier Charge (Beta)”).
  • Added: New “Apply Shipping Charges To” setting — choose which enabled payment methods the automatic courier-based shipping charge applies to (e.g. Cash on Delivery plus Direct Bank Transfer). Defaults to Cash on Delivery only, so existing setups are unchanged.

1.0.59

  • Added: Optional “Free Shipping Over (Order Value)” setting — when the order value (excluding shipping) meets or exceeds the amount you set, the courier charge is waived and shipping shows as free on Cash on Delivery orders. Leave blank to disable.
  • Note: Requires the TrackKaro server-side courier-tariff fix to be deployed for the estimate amount to appear.

1.0.58

  • Changed: The COD courier-charge estimate (Beta) now REPLACES the store’s normal shipping charge instead of being added on top of it. When Cash on Delivery is selected and a destination city is chosen, the courier estimate becomes the shipping cost (shown as a single shipping line); the store’s flat rate / free shipping still apply normally for all other orders.

1.0.57

  • Fixed: On Cash on Delivery, the Town/City field disappeared with no city dropdown in its place (the dropdown only appeared after enabling “Ship to a different address”). The city dropdown now correctly replaces whichever address’s city field is active — billing by default, or shipping when shipping to a different address.

1.0.56

  • Fixed: The checkout COD courier-charge estimate (Beta) never appeared even when fully enabled and configured — the plugin read the server config from the wrong response level, so the Leopards city dropdown and estimate line stayed hidden. The dropdown now shows correctly on Cash on Delivery selection.

1.0.55

  • Added: Optional (Beta) estimated courier charge at checkout for Cash on Delivery orders. When enabled in Settings and configured per-courier in your TrackKaro panel, customers choosing COD see a Leopards city dropdown and a live shipping charge estimate before placing their order. Off by default. The checkout dropdown only appears once the feature is fully confirmed active on the TrackKaro server — stores mid-setup (Settings box checked but panel not yet configured) see the normal WooCommerce checkout with no change.

1.0.54

  • Added: You can now create Sonic/Trax COD bookings directly from the WooCommerce order screen, just like PostEx and Leopards — select destination city and pickup address, and the shipment is booked with Trax automatically.

short_description: Auto-sync WooCommerce orders with PostEx, Leopards, TCS, CallCourier, Sonic, DEX & Daewoo FastEx. Real-time courier tracking for Pakistani stores.
description:
TrackKaro is a serviceware plugin. It connects your WooCommerce store to the TrackKaro platform (https://trackkaro.pk), an external paid SaaS service operated by DANGO Solutions. All courier API connections, status polling, and tracking data processing happen on the TrackKaro servers — not locally on your WordPress installation. A TrackKaro account is required; new accounts include a free trial.

Pakistani e-commerce stores lose hours every week manually checking courier websites and copy-pasting tracking numbers into order notes. TrackKaro fixes that.

Connect your WooCommerce store once, and TrackKaro automatically polls your courier APIs in the background, updates every order’s status, notifies your customers, and marks orders complete the moment a delivery is confirmed — all without you lifting a finger.

Supported Couriers:

  • ✅ PostEx
  • ✅ TCS
  • ✅ Leopards Courier
  • ✅ CallCourier
  • ✅ Sonic / Trax
  • ✅ DEX (Daraz Express) — tracking only
  • ✅ Daewoo FastEx
  • ✅ M&P Courier

A free TrackKaro account is required. Sign up at trackkaro.pk to start your free trial.

Why TrackKaro?

Pakistan’s courier APIs are fragmented, inconsistent, and go down without warning. TrackKaro’s server layer normalises statuses across all couriers into one clean format, handles retries, and keeps your store’s data accurate even when a courier API is having a bad day. You get dedicated tracking infrastructure without building or maintaining any of it yourself.

Key Features:

Automatic Status Sync

TrackKaro polls your couriers in the background via WP-Cron. Statuses update from “In Transit” to “Out for Delivery” to “Delivered” automatically — no manual refreshes.

Branded Customer Tracking Page

Every order gets a tracking page on your own domain. Customers click the link in their order email and see the full delivery timeline — your store name, your colours, your brand.

Real-Time Leopards Push Updates

Leopards Courier can push status updates to TrackKaro the moment they happen (no polling lag). Your orders update within seconds of a courier scan.

Courier Order Creation

Create shipment bookings with PostEx and Leopards directly from the WooCommerce order screen — COD, prepaid, and zero-value orders all supported. No need to log into courier portals.

Bulk Tracking Import

Got a spreadsheet of tracking numbers? Import them all at once via CSV. TrackKaro creates jobs for each one and starts syncing immediately.

Auto-Complete Orders on Delivery

When a parcel is delivered, TrackKaro can automatically mark the WooCommerce order as Completed.

Order List Tracking Column

See every order’s live courier status right in the WooCommerce Orders list.

Dashboard Widget

A quick-glance widget on your WordPress dashboard shows active shipments, deliveries this month, and your delivery rate.

Customer Status Email Notifications

Optionally send automated email updates to customers when their parcel moves to key milestones (dispatched, out for delivery, delivered). Works via TrackKaro’s mail server or your own SMTP.

HPOS Compatible

Fully compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (custom order tables). Tested with WooCommerce 5.0 through 9.x.

How It Works:

  1. Install the plugin and activate it on your WooCommerce store.
  2. Sign up for a free TrackKaro account at trackkaro.pk (takes 2 minutes).
  3. Copy your API token from the TrackKaro dashboard and paste it into WooCommerce → TrackKaro Settings.
  4. Done. Add a tracking number to any order and TrackKaro takes it from there.

Your free trial includes a set number of tracking jobs so you can test with real orders before subscribing.

Pricing:

TrackKaro uses a prepaid credit model billed in PKR. Buy a plan that fits your monthly order volume. No hidden fees. No long-term contracts. See current plans at trackkaro.pk.

External Services

This plugin is SERVICEWARE. It has no standalone tracking functionality — it is a connector to the TrackKaro external platform. All courier tracking, status polling, API calls to courier companies, and shipment management are processed exclusively on TrackKaro’s servers. None of this processing can be replicated locally by the plugin code itself.

A paid account with TrackKaro is required. New accounts receive a free trial, but continued use requires a prepaid PKR credit plan purchased at https://trackkaro.pk. The API key that connects this plugin to the service is obtained only after signing up.

This plugin connects to the TrackKaro platform (operated by DANGO Solutions, https://solutions.dango.pk) to provide all courier tracking and order management functionality. This connection is mandatory — the plugin cannot function without it, as all courier API communication and data processing occurs on the TrackKaro servers, not locally on your WordPress site.

Service details:

  • Service name: TrackKaro
  • Service URL: https://trackkaro.pk
  • API endpoint: https://trackkaro.pk/api/v1/
  • Operated by: DANGO Solutions (https://solutions.dango.pk)
  • Privacy Policy: https://trackkaro.pk/page/privacy-policy
  • Terms of Service: https://trackkaro.pk/page/terms-of-service

What data is sent and when:

  1. On every tracking sync (every ~5 minutes for active orders): The plugin sends your WooCommerce order’s tracking number, courier name, and an internal order reference to the TrackKaro server. The server queries the courier’s API and returns the current status, location, and event history.

  2. On plugin activation and settings save: Your store’s domain and the API token you entered are sent to TrackKaro to verify the connection. No customer data is included.

  3. On courier order creation (PostEx / Leopards): When you create a shipment booking from the WooCommerce order screen, the customer’s name, phone number, delivery address, order amount, and parcel details are sent to TrackKaro, which forwards them to the courier’s booking API to create the shipment. This transmission only occurs when you explicitly click the “Generate Courier Order” button.

  4. On customer email notifications (if enabled): The customer’s email address (stored on the order) may be sent to TrackKaro’s mail server to deliver tracking update emails. This feature is off by default and must be explicitly enabled by the shop owner.

What is NOT sent: Payment details, billing addresses, card numbers, or any information beyond what is listed above. TrackKaro acts solely as a tracking and logistics coordination service.

No tracking functionality can be performed locally — this plugin is specifically designed to work with the TrackKaro external service. If you do not agree to the TrackKaro Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, this plugin is not suitable for your store.
